quests.title: Pre-Packaged Solution

dialogue.t: These results are far, far better than expected!
Even a whole company couldn't take out as many monsters as you! Based on the current situation, there's no way those monsters can escape the ruins.
How do you feel? Was it hard work?
Urgh, yeah. Those muzzle flashes aren't super bright, but Paimon still got dizzy from staring at them for too long...
No problem! A paper I once read mentioned that you can suppress the flash by installing a device at the end of the barrel. It helps lower visual fatigue when firing for long periods.
Anyway, the crisis has been averted, and we've collected enough data to ensure the next version of my cannon will be even better!
I can't thank you enough for your help, Proto-Boss — and, of course, for that of your little assistant!

And lest we forget the vital role you played, Miss Marine... The reward money has already been earmarked for our Proto-Boss, but once I've sold the cannon, I'll split the proceeds with you — fifty-fifty!
Huh? You want to split the money with me!?
I don't care much for Mora, but I wouldn't say no to some fermented Tidalga... and it needs to be wheat-based alcohol, none of that fruity nonsense.
Paimon hasn't tried fermented Tidalga before, but it sounds like it's worth a try...

dialogue.sit: You shouldn't eat just anything, Paimon.

dialogue.t: Sure — we can just swap the alcohol with Fonta! That'll do the trick!
I've never heard of this dish before... Where would I go to find it?
This sounds like a perfect opportunity to invent an "Automated Tidalga Pickler."
After all, your Automatic Breakfast Oven works wonders. You clearly have a knack for culinary devices.
Moreover, the market for this sort of food preparation device is huge. It's not like trying to sell cannons, where you need to display their exceptional performance against powerful opponents.
And you don't have to run off to dangerous areas and battle monsters and the like every time you want to test a toaster.
Hmm, you make a good point. Maybe I should try switching my focus...

That said, if I did decide to become an inventor of machines with culinary applications — let's call them kitchen "appliances" — wouldn't all my previous work go to waste? And besides... I'd no longer have any connection to the Gardes!
You...
*sigh* I guess you're right... Giving up on all your previous work isn't really your style.
Come to think of it, apart from installing Gardemeks' target identification module on our cannon, we could also have some actual Gardemeks serve as "bodyguard meks" within its unit.
With that specialized protection detail in place, we shouldn't have to worry about monsters getting into our gun's blind spots.
That way, you can combine all these machines together and sell them as a "Pre-Packaged Solution"...
Oh! That's not a bad idea! Solving all our customers' problems with one complete package... That's definitely something worth looking into!
It's like they just need to start chatting and the ideas come flowing out...
I bet if we locked them in a room together and kept them there for a few weeks, they'd come up with all sorts of new inventions!

quests.description: After a brief battle, you manage to suppress the monsters in the ruins, collecting a large amount of data on Frejus’s cannon in the process…
